title: The early bus

item.name: The last bus
item.line: The 10.30 from the stop outside the hall. After a late night it is the only way home for half the street.

brief: The card from the ballot box has a lantern drawn on it, like the one on the spoon's hooks. Nobody on the committee will say whose it is, and the street has a louder complaint.
On the night of the final the last bus left Lantern Row at 10.21 pm. The timetable says 10.30. 14 people walked home.
The driver says he left by the hall clock, as he has for 11 years, and that the hall clock was fast.
The clock is right this morning. 1 man and 1 alibi, and the alibi is a clock. What happened to it?

suspects.name: Kwame
suspects.line: Has driven the last bus for 11 years. Never early and never late, until the night of the final.
suspects.says: I left when the hall clock said half past 10. Go and blame the clock.

steps.thing: The secretary's photos of the final. Her phone stamped each one with its own time, and the hall clock is in the back of every picture.
steps.fact: At 9.58 pm by the phone, the hall clock reads 9.58. It was right 23 minutes before the bus left by it. The face is 4 metres up, behind glass.
steps.lead: No clock gains 9 minutes in 23. Somebody moved the hands, and nobody reaches that face from the floor. Mr Cole says a clock that high is not set from a ladder. Look in the alley.

steps.thing: A hatch in the hall's back wall. The clockmaker's label is stuck inside its glass, so from the alley it reads back to front.
steps.text: .etunim eno ,nrut enO .dor eht dniw dna hctah yella eht nepo ,sdnah eht tes oT
steps.fact: The clock is set from outside: a rod behind a hatch with no lock. 1 turn moves the hands 1 minute. It is 60 paces from the bus stop, so walking there, 9 turns and walking back take 3 minutes.
steps.lead: On the ledge inside the hatch is a paper cup with a number inked on its base: 31. The tea kiosk by the stop numbers every cup it sells.

steps.thing: The kiosk's till roll. Every cup is on it, with its number and its time, because the owner pays for cups by the sleeve.
steps.fact: Cup 31 was sold at 10.04 pm, the only cup sold after 9.58. The owner remembers who to: the last bus had stood at the stop since 9.50, and its driver came over for tea.
steps.lead: Kwame does not deny the tea. He says he was out of his cab for 4 minutes and no longer, and that 4 minutes is nothing like enough.

steps.thing: His claim, set against the tape measure and the clock. 2 things already on the board bear on it, and only 1 of them decides it.

claim.says: I was out of my cab for 4 minutes. Nobody gets to that clock and back in 4.

facts.text: The clock face is 4 metres up.
The hatch is 60 paces off. There, 9 turns and back: 3 minutes.

steps.fact: It could be done. 3 minutes is enough, and he was gone for 4.
steps.lead: He could have. That is not why. Behind his sun visor is a postcard that reads oddly.

steps.thing: A postcard kept behind the sun visor. Its words say one thing to a passenger and another to whoever it was meant for. He kept the copy.
steps.text: Half light suits the hotel evening shift. Come, Etta, the music locker is open.
steps.fact: Read word by word, it says: "Her flight lands at eleven. I will meet it. Show me the clock." His daughter flew home that night, for the first time in 6 years.
steps.lead: A hatch, a cup, 4 minutes and a flight at 11. 3 accounts of that night are going round the stop. Only 1 can be true.

steps.thing: 3 accounts of the same night, as the stop is telling it. Each piece of evidence already on the board strikes 1 of them out.

accounts.text: Somebody else turned the rod as a prank on the final, and he was fooled like everybody else.
He put the clock on 9 minutes himself while the bus stood at the stop, and then left by it.
The hall clock ran fast all evening, and he left by it in good faith.

steps.fact: Chance: 4 minutes out of the cab. Means: the alley hatch, 9 turns of the rod. Motive: a flight landing at 11.

ending.found: The hall clock was put on 9 minutes just after 10 pm and put back before dawn. Cup 31 was still on the ledge. At 11.05 pm Kwame was at the airport gate, holding a card with his daughter's name on it.
ending.confession: 6 years since she left. The depot does not swap a Friday. I told myself 9 minutes hurts nobody, and I did not count the walk home.
ending.after: The depot will decide about his Fridays. He drove 3 of the 14 home himself the next night, off the clock. Asked how he knew about the hatch, he says a card came under his wiper: a drawing of the rod, and a lantern.
